extracted.intended_audience: environmental journalists, prospective SEJ members, partners, sponsors, and donors
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the Society of Environmental Journalists' mission, membership eligibility, funding policy, activities, and priorities (including diversity/equity) that guide its support of environmental journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — strengthen quality, reach and viability of environmental journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: SEJ’s mission is to strengthen the quality, reach and viability of journalism that advances public understanding of environmental issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEJ supports journalism that advances public understanding of environmental issues; activities and programs should align with improving quality, reach, or viability of such coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership eligibility — professional journalists and academics
rubrics_metrics.description: SEJ is the North American membership association of professional journalists; membership includes journalists and academics working in every type of news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership is intended for working journalists and academics in news media across the U.S., Canada, Mexico and other countries; the organization emphasizes professional practitioners as its primary constituency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership exclusion — lobbyists and public relations professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: Lobbyists and public relations professionals are not eligible for membership in SEJ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While PR and lobbying professionals cannot be SEJ members, they are still able to subscribe to SEJournal and participate in SEJ’s annual conferences (subscription/participation openness noted separately). This exclusion is a boundary intended to protect independence and editorial integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding and sponsorship policy — diversified underwriting and limits on advocacy/corporate grants
rubrics_metrics.description: SEJ operating and project budgets are underwritten through foundation grants, university sponsorships, media company contributions, earned income from dues and fees, exhibit/ad space rental, and individual gifts; SEJ seeks only small grants of general support from non-media corporations and environmental advocacy groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The funding mix aims to preserve organizational independence and education-focused mission; limits on the size/role of corporate and advocacy-group grants function as a conflict-of-interest safeguard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic methods to strengthen journalism — conferences, forums, publications, training
rubrics_metrics.description: SEJ builds reputation and advances its mission through annual conferences, regional forums, publications, online services, workshops and training sessions, and an extensive membership network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs and events should provide education, networking, and professional development that improve coverage of environment-related issues; these formats are the primary mechanisms SEJ uses to raise quality and reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprofit educational role — support for journalists covering complex environmental issues
rubrics_metrics.description: As a 501(c)(3) nonprofit educational organization, SEJ provides educational opportunities and vital support to journalists of all media who face the challenging responsibility of covering complex environmental issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities and resources are framed as educational and supportive rather than advocacy for specific policy positions; the 501(c)(3) status shapes permissible activities and the organization's public-facing posture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity, Equity and Inclusion priority — coverage of marginalized communities
rubrics_metrics.description: SEJ's Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Committee fosters and promotes greater coverage and understanding of environmental issues that affect minority and other marginalized communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stated organizational priority is to encourage and improve reporting on environmental issues impacting marginalized groups; programs, trainings, and editorial guidance should reflect DEI commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access policy — subscriptions and conference participation open to non-members
rubrics_metrics.description: Although membership has eligibility limits, all are welcome to subscribe to SEJournal and participate in SEJ's annual conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEJ distinguishes between membership (restricted) and participation/subscription (open), allowing broader engagement with SEJ publications and events while maintaining member standards.
